flashcard_questions.a: The widening difference in levels of development between the world's richest and poorest countries.

flashcard_questions.q: What are tariffs in international trade?
flashcard_questions.a: Taxes added to the cost of imported or exported goods.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do landlocked countries such as Nepal find trading difficult?
flashcard_questions.a: They have no coastline, so no access to ports for exporting goods.

flashcard_questions.q: How does malaria hold back development in tropical regions?
flashcard_questions.a: It makes people too ill to work or attend school, so they earn less.

flashcard_questions.q: How many barrels of oil does Shell extract each day globally?

flashcard_questions.a: When countries borrow more money to pay off old loans, falling deeper into debt.

flashcard_questions.q: Which country borrowed heavily after gaining independence from Portugal in 1975?
Between 1998 and 2003, developing countries paid $____ billion in debt repayments.
What is colonialism as a cause of uneven development?
flashcard_questions.a: When a powerful country controls weaker nations and exploits their resources for its own wealth.

flashcard_questions.q: How much diamond-trade revenue was lost to corruption in Zimbabwe?
flashcard_questions.a: Over $1 billion owed to the government.

flashcard_questions.q: How many people were displaced by the civil war in Sudan?
What are remittances in the context of migration?
flashcard_questions.a: Money sent back to their home country by workers who have migrated abroad.

flashcard_questions.q: What is meant by brain drain?
flashcard_questions.a: When highly qualified people leave a country, creating a shortage of skilled workers at home.

flashcard_questions.q: What share of nurses leave Ghana each year?
Nurses in Ghana earn around £150 a month; the same role in the UK pays around £____ a month.

notes: 15 cards: 6 term-to-definition from the glossary in the forward direction only (development gap, tariffs, debt treadmill, colonialism, remittances, brain drain), 5 case-study-to-fact with one figure each and the place named (Shell, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Sudan, Ghana), 2 cause-to-consequence (landlocked Nepal, malaria), 2 cloze on statistics (debt repayments, UK nurse pay). Employment-structure (primary vs tertiary) and the wealth-inequality consequence were trimmed to stay within 15 cards.
